source.title: Renaming a node rewrites `$node.<Name>` references to nodes whose name starts with it

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

When a node is renamed, n8n rewrites the expressions that reference it (`Workflow.renameNodeInParameterValue` → `applyAccessPatterns` in `packages/workflow/src/node-reference-parser-utils.ts`). The pattern for dot notation has no boundary after the old name:

```ts
replacePattern: (s) => String.raw`(\$node\.)${s}(\.?)`,
```

so renaming `Code` also matches the start of `$node.Code1`, `$node.CodeX` or `$node.Code_old` and rewrites those references too, pointing them at a node that does not exist. The `$('…')`, `$node['…']` and `$items('…')` patterns end in a quote, so they are not affected.

Default names make this easy to hit: two Code nodes are named `Code` and `Code1`, two Wait nodes `Wait` and `Wait1`, and `$node.Code1.json` is valid dot notation for both.

### To Reproduce

1. Add two Code nodes; they are named `Code` and `Code1`.
2. Add an Edit Fields (Set) node after them with a field whose value is `{{ $node.Code1.json.x }}`.
3. Rename `Code` to `Transform`.
4. Open the Edit Fields node: the value is now `{{ $node.Transform1.json.x }}`, which references a node that does not exist.

I have not run these steps in the editor. What I did run is the function the editor calls on rename (`useCanvasOperations.renameNode` → `workflow.renameNode`), `Workflow.renameNodeInParameterValue`, against `master` (`37ee6b940e`), renaming `Node1` to `NewName`:

```
"={{$node.Node12.data.value1}}"     -> "={{$node.NewName2.data.value1}}"
"={{$node.Node1_old.data.value1}}"  -> "={{$node.NewName_old.data.value1}}"
"={{$node.Node1.data.value1}}"      -> "={{$node.NewName.data.value1}}"   (correct)
```

The same input in `$('Node12')`, `$node['Node12']` or `$items('Node12')` form is left alone, as expected.

### Expected behavior

Renaming `Code` only rewrites references to `Code` itself; `$node.Code1` keeps pointing at `Code1`.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the rename code and confirmed with the unit-level run above; I have no user report for it. A fix with a regression test follows in a PR linked to this issue.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (WSL2)

### n8n Version

`master` at `37ee6b940e`

### Node.js Version

26.13.0

### Database

Not applicable: reproduced in `packages/workflow`, not in a running instance

### Execution mode

Not applicable: reproduced in `packages/workflow`, not in a running instance

### Hosting

self hosted (local checkout)

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The dot-notation pattern needs a boundary after the old node name; otherwise renaming `Code` also matches `$node.Code1`. A dot-path boundary should allow the valid next `.` while rejecting identifier continuations such as letters, digits, `_` and `$`. One detail to preserve: names containing characters that are not valid in dot notation are converted to bracket notation by the callback, so the boundary change should not alter that fallback. A regression case with `Code` and `Code1` would cover the reported collision.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
A negative lookahead against valid identifier characters handles this cleanly without breaking standalone references or bracket access:

**Patch Preview (First 3 lines of verified fix):**
```ts
replacePattern: (s) => String.raw`(\$node\.)${s}(?![a-zA-Z0-9_$])(\.?)`,
# ... [TRUNCATED — Full production patch & verification steps locked below]
```
